newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: SOCCER-ARGENTINA END BRAZIL GOAL FEAST.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ARGENTINA END BRAZIL GOAL FEAST.

text.p: Brazil's goal-scoring spree at the world youth soccer championship came to a shuddering halt on Sunday when they lost 2-0 to defending champions Argentina in the quarter-finals.
Goals from Lionel Scaloni and Martin Perezlindo in the last 12 minutes ended Brazil's stunning run in the tournament, which had seen them score 25 goals in their previous four games.
"Brazil and Argentina are always at a similar level of football," said Argentina coach Jose Nestor. "Argentina had the advantage today. We played very strongly to prevent Brazil from scoring.
"We had two chances to score and we took them. We are moving closer and closer to the title because we are united."
Brazilian coach Antonio Barroso said his side failed to make the most of their chances in the match played in Kuching on Borneo island.
"In football there is no fairness but only a winner and a loser," said Barroso. "Brazil came here to show why we are four-time champions. We did that and we won the love of the people of Kuching."
They next face the Republic of Ireland, who beat Spain 1-0.

Ghana, who won the World Under 17 title two years ago, needed a golden goal from striker Peter Ofori-Quaye six minutes into extra-time to see off the challenge of Asia's last remaining representative, Japan. The two sides were level at 1-1 at full-time.
Ghana will face Uruguay in Wednesday's other semifinal at the Shah Alam stadium near Kuala Lumpur.
Uruguay had ousted European champions France in a penalty shoot-out, after both sides were level at 1-1 after extra-time.
